verdict.rationale: Highnote's own spend rules and velocity controls are configured once and then automatically permit or restrict transactions at every authorization with no manual step, and its agentic-commerce page says cards close automatically when a workflow ends. These are narrow, payment-specific automations, not a general facility for defining arbitrary background jobs. Missing for 10: a general-purpose automation or workflow builder, scheduled or recurring jobs, event-triggered actions beyond authorization rules, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Spend rules let you automate logic on authorizations that permit or restrict transactions.
Set rules once at the program level and they apply uniformly across every card. One policy layer, enforced at scale.
Each card closes automatically when the workflow ends. No manual provisioning.
Velocity controls allow time boundary constraints to be applied to a spend rule.
